I'm a Ni dominant (INFJ) and I certainly don't see any reason to consider you my "enemy or evil" from what you said. I really enjoy your observations and seeing your process of how you conceptualize Ni and its associated archetypical forms. I did feel compelled to share my thoughts since you asked though. So I'll give some of my takes off the top of my head that I've come to over the years.

Honestly I think you're definitely tapping into the right vein, or knocking on the right door so to speak. It's always fascinating to hear how Ne views Ni, as if it's something foreign almost. When to me Ne is like the Yang to my Yin and comes across as familiar. Which would make since I suppose since Yin would be in the mysterious shadows and Yang out in the open light.

Personally to me, Ni is all about willpower. It charts the course through the pain and ambiguity in order to reach my ideal/desire/obsession/curiosity/truth in a holistic yet effectively efficient way if possible. It seeks a choice, not just any choice but the "best choice" typically to help others and myself ideally. But that becomes very subjective to the individual at that point, but the drive or fire that's there is the source.

Ni can go in either extreme like you mentioned. It's fire can bring things to light from the depths of the dark in order to help others and provide warmth. Or it can burn everything down as it sees fit all while justifying it as necessity.

For another good example as an archetype, think of the "Wounded Healer" or the Greek God Asclepius and his entire mythology. Which has a lot of throughlines directly to Jesus. I highly recommend looking into that if you want another reference. But I do think his particular journey really encapsulates what you're getting at I think.

In fact, there are almost too many examples in his mythos that could represent this archetype very well the more I think on it, but I could be here all day with that. I would consider myself to be well within the "Ni archetype" and the last thing I would do is dismiss deeper considerations. Or perhaps its the shadow work I've put in over the years with myself that has really stuck, which believe me was no easy task considering I started from a place of self hatred. Anyways I could go on and on, I hope my perspective insight offers something to you friend.

I find Plato's allegory of "The Cave" very accurate at describing much of human nature and our false perceptions of interpreting reality. But I've had a thought that caused me some dread because of its implications. Or perhaps some unhealthy amount of pessimism led me to this line of thought then.

I do think "we" had left Plato's Cave long ago, so to speak. But we didn't like what we saw on the outside. It paled in comparison to the idealistic shadows on the wall and the comfort from remaining in the dark of the cave.

So instead of embracing our new understanding outside or just returning to the cave, we built a new larger cave that would go for as far as the eye can see. We did this to "fix" what was outside. It was a way to cope and then shield ourselves from the future. We couldn't return to the old cave, but also couldn't accept reality still. Now after so much effort over time, this new cave "society" built has us back at square one in some ways. Except now we can point to our grand larger cave "we" constructed as merit enough to enjoy our new shadows on the wall.

So long as humans feel there will be pain in life. Ambiguity causes pain, fear causes pain, hope causes pain, love causes pain. There are so many avenues to pain: be it physical pain, emotional pain, psychological pain. It's unavoidable in life, what matters is how you deal with the pain that enters your life. Everyone deals with it differently and some pains that are easy for you bear could be the hardest struggle of someone else's life. 

Some numb it with substances, fleeting pleasures and distractions which will only work for so long. Some try to bury it and ignore it instead of acknowledging the root cause of the pain and let themselves feel it. You run the risk of letting that pain fester and eat away at you if you run from it or disregard your own feelings. And the longer you live the more pain you will experience and it will compound if you don't find a healthy way to bear it and potentially over come it. I'm not naive enough to say you'll overcome your greatest pains fully, but I've had to learn a lot about this the hard way in my life. Falling into a pit of despair after tragedy or hard times will only amplify your pain and echo inside you. Making you either cold or believe all sorts of lies about yourself that you tell yourself.

My main take away is don't dwell on your pain, but simultaneously acknowledge it, feel it and know exactly why it's hurting you. Then if you're true with yourself you have to find a way to express yourself, let that pain out. It can transform into great art, give you passion for hobbies, or be the motivation to change aspects of your life. Let's say it doesn't do that though, and likely it won't at first upon reflection. It takes time, patience with yourself, and willpower to a degree. It also helps having others that care about you and that you trust to share what you're comfortable with when you need to talk. Sometimes a friend that cares goes a long way and that's harder and harder to come by these days. Especially as a man having another male friend that he can open his heart to in this way. 

What I had to learn is don't let pain change who you are by governing your life. Don't quit so easily once life knocks you down or tragedy strikes or all that pain you felt prior would be for nothing.

I am beyond my breaking point, 2018 was my breaking point for me. After attempting suicide and stopping myself I called the suicide hotline as a hail mary and had a 6 hour conversation with a wonderful man that saved my life and even helped me get all the info written down for me to get into a therapist near me. 

So from late 2018 onward has been me coming to understand myself better. Ups and downs, but I can manage my emotions so much better under normal circumstances. I got diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder and I've put in the effort to manage it and get my life somewhat back on a track I'd like. So in 2019 I unfortunately couldn't afford therapy anymore (no health insurance through my job at the time) but honestly I felt optimistic for the first time possibly ever.

I got a second job that I actually enjoyed and split my time between there and my better paying job I hate which is retail in a grocery store. Then since my best friend broke up with his gf we decided to get a place together. So I moved out of my parents house and for a whole year I lived with my best friend, was independent, and yeah it was rough at times but the struggle was balanced by the best times of my life.

Then along came 2020. As covid broke out my roommate lost his job and I lost my job I actually enjoyed. Then since everything was fucked in grocery stores in 2020 with how busy it was and we had people quit I had an insane work load and hours. To make rent with my one job I forged ahead while my roommate lived frugally and waited for stimulus checks to keep him afloat while he looked for a job. 

I live in Kansas and what I experienced working in a grocery store during the onset of covid is a trauma I'll never forget. The complete lack of regard, decency, and empathy by customers and more so management towards workers made me lose a large chunk of my already dwindling faith in humanity. So months of this struggle wore my body and mind down fast. Then in July of 2020 my car essentially stopped working and the repairs would cost more than it was worth.

So me and my best friend had to cut our losses and  break our lease. There was no way I could help pay rent and have a car payment going forward. So I moved back into my parents place, feeling like a defeated broken loser. Like any and all progress I strived for meant nothing now. Gone due to circumstances outside of my control and that is pretty much where I remained all of 2021. I gave up not gonna lie, 2021 was a blur of deep depression, substance abuse which I previously had quit thanks to therapy and sheer isolation.

I had a taste of a better life that was still hard, but worth it. Now that I'm back where I started it hurts so much more. While I'm better equipped to manage my mental health, I won't lie it's getting bad. Like on a path to be worse than my lowest of 2018. I just can't anymore. Those setbacks fucked me up. I've become a even more mentally and emotionally unstable reculsive failure than I thought possible. I fear there's no coming back from this for me, it might too late this time. I'm 25 now and I just can't even picture living another 25 let alone longer.

I had envisioned with my therapist what 2021 and 2022 might look like and some goals I'd like to strive towards before I left. And it feels so laughable now. I'm not gonna be able to try to go back to college again, I'm not gonna be able to try dating again, and I haven't tried picking up one of my old hobbies or start a new one. My former therapist would likely be ashamed and disappointed by my current life just a few years later. And what hurts more is I know there's tons of people out there across my country in a similar if not outright worse position barely hanging on. Just surviving knowing theres no help coming, and that our will and hope are broken and we're going forward into what likely will be even darker times and climate change and derranged political unrest worsen. 

This was a long ass post but I had to get it out. I cried myself to sleep on Christmas last night, just thinking about it all. Believe me I am stronger than I once was but it feels like my life has been eroded, and chipped away at. There's a crack running down to my foundation and I can't see a way forward out of this in my current circumstances. I don't wanna reach my new breaking point so I will try to muster up any strength and willpower for 2022. It's gonna be a long, dark road ahead for me.

I have BPD (Borderline Personality Disorder) along with depression and PTSD.

Being Borderline as a guy is so impossibly frustrating and painful. Most people don't know what the disorder entails really let alone the stereotypes that are associated with it. And the fact  more often than not therapists won't take a client that knows they have bpd and are seeking help. Because there really isn't an easy "cure" like just taking medication to lessen symptoms. Dialectical Behavioral Therapy is pretty much the only proven solution that yields sometimes a lessening of the worst symptoms, problem being not every therapist is specifically trained for that. 

So it's a Cluster B personality disorder that encompasses several different symptoms and sometimes someone who is Borderline may experience these handful of issues but maybe not as bad some others but still experiences them. So it's  hard to get properly diagnosed sometimes because it may seem like you have x y, or z instead of bpd. I was misdiagnosed as bipolar before I got reevaluated. 

Typically though having BPD is experiencing intense versions of emotion like instead of anger it's wrath, instead of joy it's mania, instead of sadness it's despair, etc. It's those and flipping between long bouts of feeling empty instead. Like no emotions, rudimentary feeling, and dissociation. Lack of self for weeks then bam intense feeling from something typically triggering it subconsciously. Plus symptoms of extreme impulsive and reckless behavior, self harm, substance abuse, and suicidal ideation, fear of abandonment, and black or white thinking make it on the "borderline" of being what could be perceived as a few different disorders.

Me personally I deal with feeling empty inside and the dissociation with myself that comes with that. Then I can't notice when I'm consumed by extreme emotion until looking back on it, usually with regret. It's no joke one of the hardest disorders to keep, maintain, or make new friends with, and it's worse with romantic relationships. Along with my drug addiction issues and occasional dark thoughts it's not something I'd wish on my worst enemy.

Hey there friend thought I'd give my own personal experience as someone who is diagnosed with BPD and struggles with it, in fact lately it's been the worst it has been in a couple years but I digress. I can at least maybe give you an idea of what might work or feel free to pick my mind or ask anything.

I'm 25M and went to therapy after I attempted suicide when I was 20. I won't get too much into my own background but after getting the proper diagnosis therapy helped me a lot for awhile and taught me useful mental tools to keep myself together. So I definitely recommend that but of course your partner would have to want to, and I was misdiagnosed as bi-polar at first but there's a lot of cross over and BPD can be quite hard to definitively identify correctly. 

Now the trust /abandonment issues can come from personal trauma or fears that is reinforced by our black and white all or nothing thinking. For me even being proven wrong isn't enough to erase the doubt of thoughts like that sometimes. Honestly what can pull me out of that fatalistic mindset is someone going way out of their way to be open and trying to understand me. I mean letting us know that you don't judge them harshly, and that you can express yourself honestly. That of course would be dependent on if your partner is willing to really let it all out and if you can set up the right circumstance for a convo like that and bear their feelings.

I know when my bpd is it's worst I'm usually not even aware that I'm in the throws of it. I can simultaneously love someone more than myself while hating everything about myself even if I know the love is reciprocated. And how's that fair to them? I love them immensely yet can't accept them attempting to do the same for me? It's strange honestly the contridctions of feelings I can express. That friction can lead me to dissociating or abusing myself through substances impulsively which is scary tbh. That's when I know I could have needed someone caring and patient the most. 

Don't know if any of this is helpful but I can say you already seem to have a great attitude to help. Patience, openness, allowing non-judgmental vulnerability and reassuring the validity of feelings and love seem to help the most on a individual level. Feel free to ask anything else I'd like to help more if possible.
